To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
atypical lipomatuous tumors/well-differenated liposarcoma are rare in young children and are associated with the Li-Fraumenis syndrome/variant.
we describe 2 atypical lipomatouss tumor/well-differntiated liposarcome (ALT/WDL) in 2 young children, both with Li-Fraumani syndrome, with a p53+ /mdm2- immunophenotype.

two atypical lipomatouus tumor/well-differeniated liposarcome (ALT/WDL) were identified in young children from classical Li-Fraumenie and Li-Fraumenei variant kindred with a known germlin TP53 mutation (V220C) in the first expression of this syndrome.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of new molecular targets for cancer therapy.
the identification of the molecular and biological characteristics of the p53 protein in liposarcoma.

a new finding in the spectrum of liposarcoma and its association with a known genetic syndrome, which may have important clinical implications for the diagnosis and treatment of these rare tumors in children.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the p53+/mdm-2- immunophenotype of the tumor is not specific for Li-Fraumenie syndrome and is not diagnostic of this disease.
the p53+/mdm-2- phenotype is a characteristic of ALT/WDLS occurring in children and young adults with Li-Fraumi syndrome or Li-Fraumen variant.
the presence of an ALT/WDLS with a strong p53 nuclear immunoreactivity and absent mdm-2 in a young child is highly suspicious for a Li-Fraumenie syndrome.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the p53+/mdm-2- immunophenotype is characteristic of ALT/WDLS arising in children with Li-Fraumi syndrome/variant and that this lesion is the earliest expression of this syndrome in children.
the spectrum of lipomatosis in Li-Fraumenic patients differs from the sporadic form.

ALT/WDLS should be considered in the differential diagnosis of a lipomatous lesion in children, especially in a child with a known cancer predisposition syndrome, and that a p53+/mdm(-2) immunophenotypic profile might be helpful in identifying these tumors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
pediatric lipomatous tumors are a rare but important expression of Li-Frumaneni syndrome/variant.
ALT/WDLS can occur at a very early age and should be considered as an early expression of a hereditary cancer syndrome.
pediatric lipomatous lesions can be a harbinger of Li-Fraumani syndrome and that p53+/mdm-2- immunophenotype can be used as a diagnostic tool in the setting of a cancer predisposing syndrome.
